title: Aaron McKibbin and Joshua Morizono reach World Para Championships finals as Rob Davies takes bronze
seo_title: World Para Championships: McKibbin and Morizono in finals
description: Aaron McKibbin and Joshua Morizono will play for world titles in Pattaya on Thursday, while Rob Davies lost his semi-final to Chile's Vicente Leiva and took bronze.
standfirst: McKibbin saved his best for the class 8 semi-final against a 17-year-old Italian, Morizono swept aside the man who had just ended Laurens Devos's 11-year unbeaten run, and Davies's wait for a world title goes on.
body: Aaron McKibbin and Joshua Morizono will both play for world titles in Pattaya on Thursday after winning their semi-finals at the World Para Championships, while Rob Davies lost his and goes home with bronze.

McKibbin beat Italy's 17-year-old Ludovico Bini 3-1 in the men's class 8 semi-finals, winning three tight games after losing the first. Morizono beat France's Lucas Didier 3-0 in class 9, hours after Didier had ended Laurens Devos's 11-year unbeaten run.

Bini, the world No 11, had knocked out China's Zhao Shuai in the quarter-finals and took the opening game 12-10. McKibbin levelled 11-8, then won the third 12-10 and the fourth 14-12 to reach the final.

It completes a turnaround for the 34-year-old Londoner, who spent two days in bed with illness at the start of the championships and pulled out of the men's doubles with Morizono, as Eleven [reported on Tuesday](/news/world-para-championships-2026-bayley-loses-title-yan-shuo-mckibbin-medal.html). On the way he beat Israel's Yehonatan Levi 3-1 and then the Ukrainian world No 7 Maksym Nikolenko, a Paralympic bronze medallist in Tokyo and Paris, 3-2, the decider settled when Nikolenko's backhand went long at 11-10.
"It's crazy," McKibbin said, and called it the greatest achievement of his career and his best result at a major championship. His opponent in the final is Russia's Artem Iakovlev, the world No 10.
## Morizono into a second world final

Morizono, 26, who lives in Tokyo and won silver at the last world championships four years ago, came from a game down to beat Ukraine's Lev Kats 3-1 in the quarter-finals, 9-11, 11-6, 12-10, 11-9. Kats is the world No 11, a European bronze medallist and a world and European doubles champion.

The semi-final against Didier, the world No 8, was more one-sided. Didier had beaten Devos 11-6, 11-8, 11-7 in the quarter-finals, the Belgian's first singles defeat in class competition since the 2015 Belgian Open and his first ever at a world championships. Morizono, who had won all seven of their previous meetings, took it 11-6, 11-9, 11-9.
He meets Australia's Ma Lin in the final, a repeat of the 2022 Commonwealth Games final, which Morizono won in five games playing for Wales.

Davies, 42, the Rio 2016 Paralympic champion, had hoped to add the one major title missing from his career. Chile's Vicente Leiva, the 24-year-old Para Pan American champion, won the first two games of their class 1 semi-final 11-7 and 11-5. Davies took the third 11-8, but Leiva won the fourth to win 3-1.
There is no bronze medal match in Pattaya, so Davies takes bronze. He said he was "relatively happy with a bronze".

Grace Williams's run in women's class 8 ended in the quarter-finals, where she lost 3-0 to Chile's 16-year-old Florencia Perez, the world No 5 and Para Pan American silver medallist, a day after knocking out the world No 2 Mingyu Zu.
